figures.caption: Figure 3. Qualitative results on the ‘bicycle’ scene. Top to bottom: corrupted input views, our clean renders, our recovered artifact overlays, 3DGS [9], and DeSplat [26]. SSA-3DGS cleanly separates each artifact from the reconstruction, recovering both the clean scene and the artifact itself, whereas both baselines — DeSplat to a lesser extent — bake the corruption into the scene. Best viewed zoomed in on a screen.

Figure 5. Qualitative comparison on our real-world dataset against Baseline 3DGS [9] and DeSplat [26]. Each scene is shown from two viewpoints (one per row). Our method removes the genuine mud and rig occlusions while recovering clean scene geometry. Best viewed zoomed in.

Table 1. Quantitative evaluation on Mip-NeRF 360 (mean over all seven scenes). We compare vanilla 3DGS [9] trained on the corrupted images, DeSplat [26], and our SSA-3DGS, under both ADC [9] and MCMC [10] densification. DeSplat builds on a variant of ADC and is therefore listed once, under ADC. “Clean (Ref)” denotes 3DGS trained on the uncorrupted images as an upper bound. Per row and metric, the overall best result is in bold and the second best is underlined.
